issues.description: Previously the `>` comparison with default mincnt=0 guaranteed `reduce_C_function` was never called on an empty accumulator (`len(acc) > 0` required at least one point). Switching to `>=` removes that guarantee for the default/unspecified-mincnt case: `len(acc) >= 0` is always true, so empty hex bins are now passed to `reduce_C_function`. For reduce functions that don't tolerate empty input (e.g. `np.max`, `np.min`), this raises a ValueError on any hexbin call with a sparse/non-uniform data distribution and no explicit `mincnt` — a very common usage pattern. The fix addresses the mincnt>=1 symmetry with the C-is-None path but does not add a guard (e.g. `len(acc) > 0 and len(acc) >= mincnt`) to preserve the pre-existing invariant that empty bins are excluded before reduction, leaving the empty-bin edge case unresolved.
